label: Sety I builds the Hypostyle Hall
more: Sety I began the hall soon after taking the throne, setting 134 sandstone columns between Horemheb's Second Pylon and Amenhotep III's Third. Ramesses II finished the decoration. Carvings on the clerestory, made while the building ramps stood, bear Sety's name, so he, not Horemheb or Ramesses I, built it.

label: Sety I's battle reliefs
more: On the hall's north outer wall Sety I's sculptors carved his wars in Canaan, Lebanon, Syria and Libya, with the king charging alone in his chariot. The east half shows his first-year campaign; the west half later wars, including Kadesh and the Hittites. The date is about 1290 BC, within his reign.

label: Eleven Hypostyle columns collapse
more: On 3 October 1899 eleven columns of the northern wing fell in a chain reaction, and two struck the Second Pylon. Foundations of small reused blocks, crumbling in salty groundwater, could not carry the weight. Georges Legrain took the damaged columns apart and rebuilt the northern half on new foundations, finishing in May 1902.

label: Legrain finishes rebuilding the northern Hypostyle columns
more: Georges Legrain recorded the rebuilding of the northern half as complete on 15 May 1902, about two and a half years after the collapse. The columns stand on new foundations, and the southern wing was underpinned with brick while it stood.

label: Cleaning of the Hypostyle columns begins
more: In July 2021 Egyptian conservators began cleaning the hall's 134 columns, starting with the twelve central ones. Removing sand, dust and bird debris revealed colours and carved detail. In January 2024 the Supreme Council of Antiquities said 95 per cent were done.
